chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam informed us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn Aasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) that he said:
Before this Command (of the Qa'im), there will be (the risings of) al-Sufyani, al-Yamani, al-Marwani, and Shu'ayb ibn Salih. Then how does this one (Ibn Tabataba) claim this (to be the Qa'im)?

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيُّ: Al-Sufyani, a major eschatological figure who rises before the Qa'im
key_terms.الْأَمْر: The Command, referring to the rise of the Qa'im (Imam al-Mahdi)
key_terms.الْمَرْوَانِيُّ: Al-Marwani, another claimant or figure associated with the Umayyads
key_terms.الْيَمَانِيُّ: Al-Yamani, a follower who calls people to the truth before the Qa'im
key_terms.شُعَيْبُ بْنُ صَالِحٍ: Shu'ayb ibn Salih, a specific historical or eschatological figure mentioned in Shia sources

ai.seo_question: Who are the four major claimants that rise before the Qa'im according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) outlines the eschatological sequence of major claimants—Sufyani, Yamani, Marwani, and Shu'ayb ibn Salih—who must appear before the true Qa'im, thereby critiquing Ibn Tabataba's premature claim to imamate. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the 'signs' (ayat) as a chronological framework for validating the Mahdi's identity against competing pretenders. The mention of these specific figures underscores the political and spiritual turbulence characterizing the pre-appearance era in Shia eschatology.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (12) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Malik from Ali bin Aasim from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abu Nasr that Imam Abul Hasan ar-Redha (as) had said:

“Before the appearance of al-Qa’im, there will be the risings of as-Sufyani, al-Marwani, al-Yamani and Shu’ayb bin Salih. Then how does this one (Muhammad bin Ibraheem bin Issma’eel known as ibn Tabataba) claim such a thing (to be al-Qa’im)?”
